attempts.summary: Installed AIDE on node1 (RHEL 10) and established a content-aware integrity baseline for /etc. The default AIDE config only monitored permissions/ownership for /etc broadly (PERMS rule, no content hash) — strengthened it to NORMAL (adds sha512 content hashing) so file content edits are detected, not just metadata changes. Initialized the baseline database, verified a clean check, proved detection works by modifying /etc/motd and observing AIDE flag it, then reverted the test change and re-baselined to a clean state. Added a systemd service+timer for daily automated checks/reporting. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id, rebooted node1, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified the AIDE database, timer, and detection capability all survived and function correctly post-restart.
